## A Human-Centered & Harmonized Spatial Data Science Approach for Measuring Multidimensional Access to Medications for Opioid Use Disorder

Marynia Kolak\*, Paul Joudrey, Basmattee Boodram, Leslie Williams, Sam Friedman, Christina Mair

<br>

###### American Association of Geographers \| San Franciscso 2026

## Background

-   Access to medications for Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) is crucial for reducing overdoses, premature deaths, and other harms for persons who use drug (PWUD).

-   Medications like methadone and buprenorphine serve as evidence based options that can shift outcomes and save lives; but majority of persons w/OUD don’t access them

-   Structural barriers (e.g. policy variation, stigma) compound challenges like the lack of providers for diagnosing needs and/or distributing medications effectively [@smith2016]
